author: Pukujan
text: Agents keep failing visual/human UX: static numbered 1)2)3) bullets + tables instead of exercisable visuals. Growth-curve style is clearer than invented stick workers; two-line slow-vs-fast undersells Big O. Want multi-class charts (O(1) vs O(log n) vs O(n) vs O(n²)) for teach — and this must apply to every lesson/step, not one slide.

screenshot.note: Live Why step showing numbered teach list + n doubling scale; FeedbackBar (ux.feedback) visible at bottom.

promotion.note: Product critique; do not write learn.* mastery events.

author: Pukujan
text: O(1) teach still leads with numbered chrome (1. 2) 3)) over a flat table. Prefer graph/curve frames; strip digit-prefixed lists from teach copy (A19 / plain-human rewrite).

screenshot.note: O(1) step with numbered prose + flat O(1) scoreboard.

author: Pukujan
text: P0 crash: click Explain again twice → ErrorBoundary "Something broke on this screen". Console: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type'). Needs null-safe visual/presentation .type and a multi-click regression.

promotion.note: Tracked as issue #163; keep this git entry as calibration evidence even after the fix lands.

author: Pukujan
text: Curated multi-class cheatsheet charts are too complex for the live teach frame. Default to a simple 4-curve O(1)/O(log n)/O(n)/O(n²) only — full cheatsheets are reference, not the teach panel.

screenshot.note: Pack sample: dense multi-class / factorial cheatsheets — reference only.

author: Pukujan
text: Interactive pick-which-curve / draw-dots examples are research topics to investigate in the literature + external programs — not an internal quality bar. Pipeline must ground in that research (catalog-wide exercisable visuals), not reverse-engineer vibes from chat. Do not lock one hardcoded 3-graph Big O probe as the product.

promotion.note: Issue #161 comments 5853795906 / 5853799188. Decomposer pedagogy ratings still go to ux.decomposer_review when reviewing generated artifacts.

author: Pukujan
text: Wanted patterns: interactive growth graphs (click dots / point-and-drag to draw O(1) vs linear vs quadratic); learner constructs the curve then system checks shape (flat vs rising); person-counting-boxes or multi-class charts as supporting frames — not invent-first stick spam. Whole catalog: every lesson/step, not one slide.

screenshot.note: Invent-first stick-worker / number-box metaphor Pukujan rejected for teach.

author: Pukujan
text: Probe UX pick example: three graphs side-by-side (flat / linear / quadratic). Learner picks or draws which is O(1) vs O(n) vs O(n²). Axes show simple n / ops numbers only — no numbered bullet essays. This is an example of the *kind* of UX, not a locked product step.

screenshot.note: Current slow-vs-fast two-line frame undersells Big O vs multi-class / pick-which-curve.

author: Pukujan
text: Two-line slow-vs-fast growth undersells Big O. Prefer multi-class O(1)/O(log n)/O(n)/O(n²) charts in the teach frame (simple, not dense cheatsheets).

screenshot.note: Live slow-vs-fast frame with numbered captions.

author: Pukujan
text: Reject invent-first stick-worker / “workers carrying number-boxes” metaphors for Big O teach. Growth-curve style (research-backed multi-class charts) is clearer. Ground visuals in external research + real study-program artifacts — invent forbidden.

author: Pukujan
text: Why step still leads with hikers analogy + empty n=2/4/8/16 table scoreboard and numbered lists. Need real multi-class growth visuals on the teach card, not prose + blank table waiting for later steps.

screenshot.note: Hikers analogy Why step with empty counts table.

author: Pukujan
text: Hates bright lavender visuals; wants dark mode for player + teach frames. Charts must stay readable on dark. Log prefer_dark.

screenshot.note: Bright lavender player chrome that motivated dark-mode ask.

author: Pukujan
text: Not a one-off dark CSS dump — easily switchable design system (CSS tokens + theme switcher). Dark/light first; more themes later. Design tokens (color, type, space); ThemeProvider + persistent toggle; player + teach visuals consume tokens.

author: Pukujan
text: Not just dark/light — full customization: color palette packs, text/typography changes, mood presets, everything switchable via design tokens.

author: Pukujan
text: Out of scope for theme work for now: curated teach image renders + teacher pet/bot. Theme system skins chrome/UI only.

author: Pukujan
text: Attribute product UX critiques and human-feedback entries to author **Pukujan** (not Alex). Reuse existing stack: ux.decomposer_review, ux.feedback, sessions/.../sliding-window-pedagogy-calibration/ — thin adapter under content/human-feedback, no second database.

author: Pukujan
text: Pet/mascot bugs: empty one-shot frames live; no walking (slides with idle animation = shaking/jitter in place); hover semantics unclear; mobile touch UX unclear. Needs generated walk/turn frames (not CSS hacks) and a locomotion state machine so idle is not jitter.

screenshot.note: Player with companion pet visible during sliding-window probe (jitter context).

promotion.note: Durable from #121 / GOAL-2026-09-25; still open calibration for agents.

author: Pukujan
text: Comparing fractions Step 1: cannot submit a lesson answer — teach shows “Which is bigger, 3/4 or 2/3?” but probe was null so only the 1–5 review Submit appeared (easy to confuse). Step 1 should accept an answer too (not teach-only). Also no Back / LessonMap jump to other steps; blocked from advancing to Step 2.

screenshot.note: Comparing fractions Step 1 with bar visuals + Explain/Worked; probe gap called out live.

promotion.note: Human-test on live 2dbe00b; later unblocked in PR #138 — keep as calibration evidence.

author: Pukujan
text: Fractions teach/explain/worked must be number-line-first where research requires (Hamdan & Gunderson; Fuchs; IES Teaching Fractions Toolkit Module 1). Bar models OK as supporting frames; do not invent metaphors without provenance. Catalog-wide, every fractions step.

screenshot.note: IES Teaching Fractions Toolkit Module 1 overview — research source for number-line-first.

author: Pukujan
text: Fractions denominator step uses equal-parts bar (“denominator = 4”) with numbered teach chrome risk. Keep visual primary; strip digit-prefixed essay lists; ensure Check probe + 1–5 review stay distinct.

screenshot.note: Denominator equal-parts bar + Check probe + review bar.

author: Pukujan
text: Sliding-window box/index visuals stay on the golden box_index representation — do not invent new metaphors. Still apply catalog-wide rules: no numbered teach spam, Explain again must not crash, research-first if replacing a still.

screenshot.note: Sliding window Ready step with positions/numbers boxes.

promotion.note: #161 queues sliding-window external stills; keep box_index.

author: Pukujan
text: Tutor reply latency is 18–60s+ on live — companion ack fix makes it survivable, not fast. Still a product UX defect; agents must not claim chat feels instant.

author: Pukujan
text: Worked example must visibly change content vs teach (not duplicate the same numbered prose + empty table). Numbered chrome still present on both cards.
